review_method: Independent original-map pixel inspection, complete source and baseline-rendered ring plots, registered outline and filled overlays, surrounding-map context and publication imprints. All 130 ordered positions across three single-ring Polygons were independently compared with retained source geometry, decoded geometry and exact original inventory/core/detail joins. The Manitoba GeoPDF full embedded affine, including both rotation terms, was independently reopened and all 110 selected registrations recomputed. The Saskatchewan WSA and Cumberland GeoPDF affines were independently reopened and all 20 selected positions recomputed for each map. Three retained successful acquisition receipts were verified against original bytes. Every selected position lies within an inspected original crop. First source-pixel observations and wider-context refinements were recorded before comparison with separate findings. Neither bounding boxes, nearby labels nor apparent connectivity alone established a water identity. The production decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: Resolve the intervening corridor, southwest corner and component name partitions before whole-feature scalar naming. This is a name-scope hold, not an access failure.
findings.supported_name_scope: The single selected ring combines the northern Misty Lake association and southern Lac Brochet association. These are non-exhaustive component associations. The intervening narrow corridor and southwest corner beside Kingsley Lake have no exact named-water partition established. The coarse ring crosses mapped land and omits substantial northern, western and eastern detailed continuations. Entire detailed named-lake extents remain unverified. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The single selected ring combines the northern Misty Lake association and southern Lac Brochet association. These are non-exhaustive component associations. The intervening narrow corridor and southwest corner beside Kingsley Lake have no exact named-water partition established. The coarse ring crosses mapped land and omits substantial northern, western and eastern detailed continuations. Entire detailed named-lake extents remain unverified.

Kingsley Lake lies west/southwest beside the selected corner; label proximity is not proof of a selected Kingsley component. Waspison Lake and Whiskey Jack Lake are distinct western and southwestern waters. Cochrane River is surrounding hydrographic context. None is certified as a whole-feature alias.

The Manitoba Geological Survey publication supplies the selected naming evidence for the two Manitoba targets. Two retained Saskatchewan maps provide context for the unnamed third target. Three publisher organizations are represented; underlying hydrographic dataset independence and formal naming-registry authority are unverified.
No Korean form or additional whole-feature alias is certified; registered overlays do not establish surveyed shores or exact name partitions.
